bargainingGuide.title: The Bargaining Lifecycle: From Survey to Signing
bargainingGuide.subtitle: How Local Bargaining Committees manage membership from demand setting through ratification
bargainingGuide.intro: Negotiating a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) is the most important thing your local will do. Even if your National or Provincial union sends a Staff Representative to lead the negotiations, the Local Bargaining Committee must manage the membership. Here is the standard lifecycle of contract negotiations in Canada/Ontario — plus the comms, tracking, and mandate work that keep members with you.

disclaimer.title: Not legal advice
disclaimer.body: Timelines such as notice to bargain, strike votes, and No Board countdown vary by statute and sector (Labour Relations Act vs Colleges Collective Bargaining Act, and peers). Confirm every deadline, quorum, and ballot rule with your Staff Representative and your own collective agreement before you act.

diagram.caption: Four phases every Local Bargaining Committee walks — survey to signing.

gate.title: Start here: committee, statute, and the Staff Rep
gate.intro: Before you draft a survey, know who owns the table, which Act applies, and who signs the legal letters.

sector.label: Confirm the statute
sector.content: Most Ontario private and broader-public units bargain under the Labour Relations Act. Ontario college support and faculty units often use the Colleges Collective Bargaining Act. The No Board countdown and strike rules are not identical — check which Act covers your certificate.

committee.label: Name the Local Bargaining Committee
committee.content: The committee manages membership: surveys, updates, strike votes, and ratification logistics. The Staff Representative may lead at the table; the local still owns the mandate.

rep.label: Partner with the Staff Representative
rep.content: Notice to bargain, conciliation applications, and legal timelines usually run through your servicing rep. Do not invent deadlines from this page alone.

ca.label: Read your current CA
ca.content: Expiry date, renewal language, and any early-notice clauses live in your agreement. Pull the signed PDF before you calendar the survey.

gate.sectorCaption: Sector fork — confirm with your Staff Representative before you promise members a timeline.

lra.question: Who leads the legal clock?
lra.lra: Ministry of Labour conciliation and no-board under the LRA.
lra.ccba: College-sector rules under the CCBA — confirm with your national/provincial college team.

ccba.question: What changes for the local?
ccba.lra: Local still owns survey, updates, strike vote logistics, and tracker — plus Staff Rep guidance on the countdown.
ccba.ccba: Same membership jobs. Dispute timelines and central tables may differ — ask the college bargaining team before you print dates.

gate.warning: If your local posts a strike date or No Board day without confirming the statute and the mailed notice, you can put members in an illegal position. Call the Staff Representative first.

prep.title: Phase 1: Preparation & demand setting
prep.intro: Months before the contract expires, the committee listens to members and opens negotiations formally.

survey.label: The member survey
survey.content: Months before expiry, survey members on priorities — wages, sick days, scheduling, safety, workload. Pair the survey with workplace mapping so quiet departments are not invisible.

demand.label: Demand setting
demand.content: The committee reviews survey results and drafts the initial proposals the union will table. Rank must-haves vs stretch items before you meet the employer.

notice.label: Notice to bargain
notice.content: A formal legal letter to the employer (often about 90 days before expiry under many Ontario paths) officially opens negotiations. Route it through your Staff Representative.

prep.tip: A strong survey without a membership list is noise. Clean the roster and sign up missing members before you ask for a mandate.

table.title: Phase 2: The table
table.intro: Both sides meet, exchange proposals, and keep members engaged without breaking table discipline.

exchange.label: Exchanging proposals
exchange.content: Both sides meet and exchange their lists of demands. Log every article the day it moves — not the week after.

blackout.label: Table discipline (the blackout)
blackout.content: Usually, detailed table talk stays in caucus until a tentative agreement. That does not mean silence: members still need regular Bargaining Updates that stay factual and on-message.

tracking.label: Tracking
tracking.content: Track every proposal, counter, and sign-off. Keep strategy off employer servers — use the on-device Proposal Tracker and export CSV to a USB drive after each session.

table.tip: If the employer leaks a half-story, answer with one shared fact sheet — not a chat thread of competing rumours.

comms.title: Blackout vs Bargaining Updates
comms.intro: Table secrecy and membership mobilization are different jobs. The committee must do both.

cadence.label: Set a cadence
cadence.content: Pick a weekly or biweekly update rhythm before the first table day. Members should know when the next note lands even if there is "nothing new" at the table.

channels.label: Split the channels
channels.content: Email carries the durable record members can find later. Social and boards carry a short hook or photo. Keep the facts identical across channels.

facts.label: Facts only
facts.content: Say what phase you are in, what members should do next, and what is still confidential. Do not invent employer positions you cannot confirm.

crisis.label: Escalate when stakes rise
crisis.content: Strike votes, No Board, and picket logistics live in the Strike & Crisis Comms Guide — use that playbook for high-stakes messaging.

comms.tip: One message, many channels. If the email and the board notice disagree, members will trust neither.

tracker.title: How to run the Proposal Tracker
tracker.intro: Treat the tracker like the committee's private spreadsheet — on a personal device, never on employer Wi-Fi folders.

article.label: Article / section
article.content: Use the CA number members recognize (for example Article 12.01). One row per live issue.

status.label: Status discipline
status.content: Move rows to Tentatively Agreed, Withdrew, or Impasse only when the caucus agrees. Do not mark TA on a handshake you have not logged.

device.label: Device rule
device.content: Save on the committee laptop or a steward's personal phone. Do not leave open tabs on employer workstations.

csv.label: Export every session
csv.content: Export CSV to a labelled USB stick before you pack up. If the browser clears storage, the USB is the backup.

tracker.calloutBody: The tracker saves on this device only. Nothing is sent to the cloud. Export CSV to back up notes after each bargaining day.

dispute.title: Phase 3: Dispute resolution & the strike vote
dispute.intro: If negotiations stall, the legal clock starts. Membership work intensifies — this is not the time to go quiet.

diagram.caption: Typical Ontario LRA path — confirm the mailed notice date and sector rules with your Staff Representative.

conciliation.label: Conciliation
conciliation.content: A government-appointed neutral tries to help both sides reach an agreement. Either party can request it; it is usually required before a lawful work stoppage path opens.

strikeVote.label: The strike vote
strikeVote.content: The local asks members to authorize a strike if a fair deal is not reached. A strong Yes often moves the employer. Plan turnout early — a weak mandate is harder to recover from than a delayed vote.

noBoard.label: The "No Board" report (Ontario)
noBoard.content: If conciliation fails, a No Board notice is typically issued. Under many LRA paths that starts a countdown (often to the 17th day after release) before a legal strike or lockout. Confirm the exact day with your Staff Representative.

voteMechanics.label: Strike vote mechanics
voteMechanics.content: Confirm eligibility (usually members in good standing in the bargaining unit), notice period, secret ballot, scrutineers, and the majority threshold in your bylaws and Act before you call the vote. Publish the certified result once the count is finished.

dispute.warning: Do not announce a strike start date from this page. Use the mailed No Board date, your Act, and your Staff Representative. Wrong dates put members at legal risk.
dispute.ccbaBody: If your certificate sits under the Colleges Collective Bargaining Act, do not assume the LRA No Board diagram applies day-for-day. Ask your national or provincial college bargaining team for the sector clock, then keep the same local jobs: survey, updates, strike vote logistics, and tracker discipline.

ratify.title: Phase 4: Ratification and signing
ratify.intro: A deal only becomes the new agreement when members vote and both parties sign.

ta.label: Tentative Agreement (TA)
ta.content: The bargaining team reaches a deal with the employer. Publish a clear highlights package before the ratification meeting — not only a verbal summary.

national.label: National or provincial sign-off
national.content: Some constitutions require Staff Rep or executive approval of a TA before it goes to members. Confirm that step before you book the ratification room.

eligibility.label: Eligibility and notice
eligibility.content: Confirm who may vote under your bylaws and constitution, how much notice members get, and whether the ballot is in-person, hybrid, or mail. Put those rules in the first email.

ratification.label: Ratification vote
ratification.content: Members vote by secret ballot to accept or reject the TA. Confirm the majority threshold (simple majority vs two-thirds) before you print ballots.

reject.label: If members reject the TA
reject.content: A No vote returns the team to the table or to the statutory path still open. Do not invent a new deal in the hallway — caucus with the Staff Representative and update members with the next step.

signing.label: Signing
signing.content: Once ratified, both parties sign the new Collective Agreement and arrange printing or digital distribution for stewards and members.

ratify.tip: Put the vote link, meeting time, eligibility, and majority rule in the first line of the email. Members should not hunt for the mandate.
ratify.rejectTitle: Rejected TA is not failure — it is a mandate
ratify.rejectBody: Members can say No. Your job is a clean process, a clear next step, and no rumours about who "lost." Keep the tracker current and the update cadence alive.

checklist.title: Bargaining committee checklist
checklist.intro: Tick these as you move through the cycle. Print or keep them beside the tracker.

survey.label: Member survey live
survey.content: Priorities collected with enough response from every department and shift.

notice.label: Notice to bargain sent
notice.content: Legal letter dated and confirmed with the Staff Representative.

tracker.label: Tracker opened
tracker.content: Every live article has a row; status rules agreed in caucus.

updates.label: Update cadence set
updates.content: Members know when the next Bargaining Update lands.

vote.label: Strike vote plan
vote.content: Date, eligibility, notice, ballot method, majority threshold, and scrutineers locked before you need bargaining power.

noboard.label: No Board day confirmed
noboard.content: Mailed notice date and countdown verified with the Staff Representative — not guessed.

ratify.label: Ratification logistics
ratify.content: Highlights package, eligibility list, majority rule on the ballot notice, meeting room or online ballot ready.

export.label: CSV backup after each session
export.content: USB labelled with the date; one copy with the chief negotiator.

national.label: National / provincial TA clearance
national.content: If your constitution requires it, get the Staff Rep or executive letter before the member ballot.

fullScenario.title: Worked example: campus support unit, one year out
fullScenario.intro: A composite Local Bargaining Committee path. Dates are illustrative — replace them with your Act and Staff Rep calendar.

t90.label: T-90 days
t90.content: Survey closes; demand package ranked; notice to bargain drafted with the Staff Representative.

table.label: Table months
table.content: Weekly caucus; Proposal Tracker updated same day; biweekly email update to members with no table secrets.

vote.label: Strike vote week
vote.content: Clean Yes mandate; employer returns to wage package; tracker marks three articles Tentatively Agreed.

noboard.label: No Board issued
noboard.content: Committee confirms day 0 from the mailed notice; crisis comms lead takes the daily message; USB backups every night.

ratify.label: Ratification Saturday
ratify.content: National clearance confirmed Tuesday; highlights PDF emailed Thursday; secret ballot Saturday; signing Monday; stewards get printed CAs within two weeks.

fullScenario.tip: If your unit is college-sector under the CCBA, keep the same membership jobs — only the legal clock changes.

notThis.title: What this guide is not
notThis.intro: Keep jobs separate so members get the right playbook.

crisis.label: Not the Strike & Crisis Comms Guide
crisis.content: Use the Strike Guide for picket messaging, media lines, and high-stakes cadence once a work stoppage is near.

grievance.label: Not the grievance process
grievance.content: Individual contract enforcement stays on the grievance playbook. Bargaining changes the CA for everyone.

joint.label: Not joint committee recommendations
joint.content: Joint union-employer tables recommend; they do not bargain the CA. See the joint committee playbook for that lane.

wildcat.label: Not a green light for wildcats
wildcat.content: Unauthorized stoppages put members and the local at risk. Stay inside the statutory path your Staff Representative confirms.

tools.title: Tools for the bargaining cycle
tools.intro: Open these on personal devices. Keep strategy and member lists off employer systems.

tracker.label: Proposal Tracker
tracker.content: Spreadsheet of articles, counters, and status with CSV export.

email.label: Email & outreach guide
email.content: Durable Bargaining Updates and ratification vote emails.

graphic.label: Graphic Maker
graphic.content: Short social hooks that match the email facts — try the bargaining update preset.

flyer.label: Flyer Maker
flyer.content: Strike vote and ratification meeting posters for boards and entrances.

mapping.label: Workplace mapping
mapping.content: Find quiet departments before the survey so the mandate is real.

failureModes.title: What breaks a bargaining mandate
failureModes.intro: Name the failure mode early so the committee does not "fix it at the mic" after a weak vote.

turnout.label: Weak strike-vote turnout
turnout.content: A thin Yes looks soft to the employer. Fix: map departments before the vote, assign stewards to shifts, and give clear notice with the ballot method.

leak.label: Table talk leaked as rumour
leak.content: Half-quotes from caucus hit Facebook before the Bargaining Update. Fix: one fact sheet, one messenger, same words on email and boards.

noHighlights.label: Ratifying without a highlights package
noHighlights.content: Members vote on a verbal summary and feel lied to later. Fix: plain-language highlights with money, language, and what stayed status quo — emailed before the meeting.

rejected.label: No plan for a rejected TA
rejected.content: The room says No and officers freeze. Fix: agree in caucus beforehand what happens next (return to table, extend countdown, new update cadence) with the Staff Representative.

wrongDate.label: Wrong strike or No Board date
wrongDate.content: A flyer prints a date guessed from this guide. Fix: only publish dates confirmed from the mailed notice and your Staff Representative.

failureModes.tip: Most bargaining disasters are process and trust — not the wage number alone.

rulesOfOrder.title: Rules of Order Cheat Sheet
rulesOfOrder.subtitle: What to say when you move, amend, or raise a point during a union meeting
rulesOfOrder.whenToUse: Open this on your phone during a general membership meeting when you need the exact wording for a parliamentary action.
rulesOfOrder.guideLink: Read the Running a Meeting guide
rulesOfOrder.pickerHeading: What do you want to do?
rulesOfOrder.pickerIntro: Tap an action below. Each card shows what to say, when to use it, and what the Chair does next.
rulesOfOrder.noResults: No actions match that search. Try "motion", "order", or "adjourn".

miniMode.title: Mini mode on the floor
miniMode.body: Search or filter, tap an action, then copy the phrase. Chair notes stay on the card so you know what happens next.

mainMotion.label: Introduce a main motion
mainMotion.hint: Use when you want the local to take a new action — donation, endorsement, policy, or expenditure.
mainMotion.chairNote: Restate the motion, open debate, recognize the mover first.

amendMotion.label: Change or edit a motion on the floor
amendMotion.whatToSay: "I move to amend the motion by [adding/striking words]…"
amendMotion.hint: Use to fix wording before the final vote — not to replace the whole idea.
amendMotion.chairNote: Vote on the amendment before returning to the main motion as amended.

callQuestion.label: Force a vote and stop debate (call the question)
callQuestion.whatToSay: "I move the previous question." OR "I call the question."
callQuestion.hint: Use when debate has run its course and the room is ready to vote.
callQuestion.chairNote: If adopted, vote on the pending motion without further debate.

tableMotion.label: Table or postpone the motion
tableMotion.whatToSay: "I move to table the motion." OR "I move to postpone this matter to the next meeting."
tableMotion.hint: Use when the local needs more information or time before deciding.
tableMotion.chairNote: If adopted, the main motion is set aside until the local brings it back.

referCommittee.label: Send the motion to a committee
referCommittee.whatToSay: "I move to refer the motion to [committee] with instructions to report back by [date]."
referCommittee.hint: Use for complex items that need research before a final vote.
referCommittee.chairNote: Specify committee and deadline in the motion before taking debate.

limitDebate.label: Limit or extend debate time
limitDebate.whatToSay: "I move to limit debate to [number] minutes per speaker."
limitDebate.hint: Use when speeches are repeating or the meeting is running long.
limitDebate.chairNote: State the time limit clearly; enforce it evenly.

divideQuestion.label: Vote on parts separately
divideQuestion.hint: Use when a motion has independent parts — e.g., two separate donations in one motion.
divideQuestion.chairNote: If adopted, vote on each part in order.

reconsider.label: Reconsider a vote
reconsider.whatToSay: "I move to reconsider the vote on [motion]."
reconsider.hint: Use on the same day or next meeting per your rules — usually by a member on the winning side.
reconsider.chairNote: Confirm timing rules in your bylaws before reopening debate.

withdrawMotion.label: Withdraw your motion
withdrawMotion.hint: Only the mover can ask to withdraw — the Chair asks if any member objects.
withdrawMotion.chairNote: If no objection, the motion is withdrawn. If any member objects, the motion stays on the floor.

pointOfPrivilege.label: Complain about noise, temperature, or a distraction
pointOfPrivilege.hint: Use for comfort, safety, or ability to hear — not to argue the motion.
pointOfPrivilege.chairNote: Rule immediately — fix the distraction or deny if not a true privilege.

pointOfOrder.label: Point out that the rules are being broken
pointOfOrder.hint: Use when procedure is wrong — wrong precedence, Chair debating, or lost quorum.
pointOfOrder.chairNote: State your ruling. A member may appeal the Chair's ruling to the assembly.

pointOfInformation.label: Ask a question about the facts of the debate
pointOfInformation.hint: Use only for urgent factual clarification — not speeches disguised as questions.
pointOfInformation.chairNote: Answer briefly or direct the question to the right officer.

adjourn.label: End the meeting
adjourn.hint: Use to close the meeting after business is done or when quorum is lost.
adjourn.chairNote: If adopted, declare the meeting adjourned and note the time.

recess.label: Take a short break
recess.whatToSay: "I move that we take a recess until [time]."
recess.hint: Use for a bathroom or caucus break without ending the meeting.
recess.chairNote: State the return time; reconvene with "The meeting will come to order."
